selected.title: He Told His Coworkers We Had an Open Relationship
selected.hook: My boyfriend told his coworkers we were in an open relationship. We are absolutely not.
selected.voiceover:
My boyfriend told his coworkers we were in an open relationship. We are absolutely not.

I found out when I joined his team for drinks after work. One coworker kept flirting with me, then laughed and said, "Relax, I know you two have an arrangement."

I asked what arrangement.

The whole table went quiet.

She looked at my boyfriend and said he'd told everyone we were "not strict about exclusivity."

We've been together for four years. We have never had that conversation.

On the way home, he said it was a joke that got out of hand. Months ago, someone teased him for never flirting back at work, so he said our relationship was "more flexible than people think."

But another coworker texted me later and said he'd repeated it several times. She also said he'd used it whenever someone questioned why he was getting too friendly with women at office events.

He insists nothing physical happened and says I'm treating workplace gossip like proof of cheating.

But that's not really the point.

For months, people who see him every day believed I had agreed to rules I never agreed to, because that story made his behavior easier to explain.

Now he wants me to forget it because "everyone knows the truth."

Would you believe nothing happened, or would the lie itself change how you see the relationship?

She thought she was walking into a normal after-work drink until one coworker's comment revealed that her boyfriend had been telling the office they were in an open relationship. He says it was only a joke and nothing physical happened, but the story had apparently been repeated for months. Is the lie itself enough to break trust?
